Subject: Post-call recap: Redwood integration & next steps

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the call earlier — super helpful. Quick recap from our side so we can confirm alignment before the technical deep-dive: 

Pain points
- Current LLM endpoint has 400-600ms center latency for single-shot requests; tail latencies spike to ~1.2s under load. This kills our product UX for streaming chat.
- Search relevancy is inconsistent. We're using embeddings + a cosine-based index but need reranking and better vector scoring for commerce queries.
- Integration complexity: our frontend expects streaming tokens and structured JSON outputs for downstream parsing.
- Cost: token costs and instance sizing are a concern and need predictable unit economics for forecasting.

Goals
- Deploy a POC that supports streaming token-level responses, function-calling for resolved intents, and structured output (JSON schema) for order extraction.
- Try Redwood's embeddings + reranking to improve search precision on our catalog.
- Get a sense of performance vs cost (latency p50/p95 and per-token pricing) for a 3-month pilot.

Next steps we discussed: tech deep-dive next week (include our infra/SRE and your engineering team), share SDK migration guidance, and a short POC scope/estimate.

Can you confirm availability Tue/Wed next week for a 60-min session and share any pre-reads?

Best,
Alex

Hi Alex,

Thanks for the clear summary. Confirming on our side and adding a few clarifications so everyone is aligned before the deep-dive: 

Confirmed pain points and how Redwood can help
- Latency: our Dedicated pools + streaming path reduce p50 latency compared to batch endpoints; we also support continuous batching with SLO-aware routing to keep tail latencies bounded. For the POC we can provision a small dedicated pool to hit p95 SLAs.
- Embeddings + reranking: Redwood Optimize can run candidate reranks using lightweight cross-encoders (on-request) or hybrid reranking with embeddings + cheap reranker for higher precision. We'll share a short eval plan.
- Streaming & structured outputs: the SDK supports chunked token streaming and a function-calling contract that returns validated JSON with schema enforcement. That should map cleanly to your downstream parsers.
- Cost controls: we'll propose batching/caching profiles, quantization options, and routing rules to balance latency vs cost.

Attachments: I'm attaching our integration-playbook.pdf with quick start steps and a short SDK migration checklist. Also including a one-pager on reranking approaches.

Thanks Alex / Marissa for the quick technical notes ahead of the deep-dive: 

1) SDK/migration
- We recently shipped client v2 (node/python) that unifies streaming and function-calling APIs. Migration is usually 1-3 dev days for a frontend that already consumes token streams. See attached sdk-migration-guide.md for code examples.

2) Streaming & function calling
- Streaming: token-by-token SSE or WebSocket streaming available; library provides incremental JSON-building helpers that can validate against a schema as tokens arrive.
- Function calling: we support both synchronous function calls (runtime triggers) and asynchronous callback patterns if you need side-effect isolation.

3) Embeddings & reranking
- Embeddings endpoint supports fixed-dim vectors and batching; we provide a reranker endpoint that accepts candidate IDs + embeddings and returns a ranked list with scores. For catalog search we recommend a two-stage approach: ANN retrieval + Redwood reranker.

4) Performance expectations (preliminary)
- POC config: 2x A10 GPUs in a dedicated pool, streaming path enabled. Expected p50 ~ 120-220ms, p95 ~ 350-550ms for <512 token responses depending on model and quantization. We'll run a short latency profile during the POC.

Agenda suggestion for deep-dive
- 10m intros & goals
- 20m infra/latency requirements & current telemetry
- 20m SDK integration demo (streaming + function-calling example)
- 10m POC scope & next steps

I've attached sdk-migration-guide.md and a small demo snippet. Happy to add any infra folks you want on the invite.
